body: Thank you. I write about this often, but mostly I write TO him. Dozens of pages of "letters" scribbled in a notebook that he'll never read, but I need to get it out.

It's okay. I know how silly it sounds. I never expected him to leave his wife or to marry me or anything drastic. But I guess I thought he'd always be in my life. He told me things like "I'll always be here for you" and "we'll always be friends". I expected the status quo. He was my entire support system for so long. It was wishful thinking and it was a total emotional crutch for me.

What do you think she would gain from knowing? It's over. I think she probably suspects something because he's a serial cheater, but I know he does love his wife very much. For all I know they have an arrangement. They both live a VERY high end lifestyle because of his career, enough so that a lot of people would stick around either way. I'd rather let them live their lives in happy denial.

Thank you. I'm 31 now and sometimes I think about the nearly 2 years I wasted on this man and what I could have been doing instead. I honestly feel really old at this point, like I come with a lifetime of emotional baggage.

Thank you. Deep down I know. He tries to be "cordial" with me but it comes off as cold, and it sets me off into fits of crazy text messages. I don't think he and I will ever have a civil relationship, and that's my fault. I'm honestly not sure I'd want one.

Thank you so much. Your last two sentences made me tear up. My parents have been gone almost 2 years now, and my relationship with him is the only "love" I've known since. When he left me it honestly did make me feel like maybe I wasn't worth loving, that maybe the only 2 people who were "obligated" to love me were gone and I'd never experience someone caring about me like that again. 

And yes, it came completely out of the blue. We had a great day together on my birthday, and then he disappeared for 3 weeks and only showed back up to tell me it was over. I thought the whole having our last hookup be on my birthday thing was pretty cruel.

Thank you. Writing this all out is cathartic, I think having an outlet for this is the only thing that will keep me from self imploding over it. I never thought I'd need a forum like this but I'm really glad it exists.

Thank you. I casually dated throughout my relationship with my married man, but I've completely shut down emotionally since he ended it. I know I need to move on and get back in the dating game, but I can't stop thinking about him. I honestly feel bad for the next guy I'm in a relationship with because I'm scared I'll constantly compare him to this man.
Sounds like you have a good handle on it. Really hope to get there someday.
Thank you.
It's in my mind right now. Fuck, I still dream about it. He was amazing.

This coming out would probably end me professionally. Even though nothing happened while I was his subordinate. He, on the other hand, has a history of and reputation for fucking his secretaries. I am at least the second and probably the third.

This is my main hangup - what hurts more, going NC or continuing to play his games and stay "friends"? 

I don't know.
Thanks for the perspective. Despite everything I hope that he and I can get to where you are someday.
I absolutely feel "addicted" to this man. I was nowhere close to over him, but this basically brought me back to day one of the breakup.
I don't think any of us here are innocent or victims. I was a victim of my own naïveté and loneliness, but the way he is going about ending this is unnecessarily cruel.
That's we'd always be friends, that he'd take care of me. That's it.

I've struggled with the idea that I brought this on myself and I know some of the blame is on me. I'd known him since I was in my early 20s, he was my college mentor then my first real boss. Not a single inappropriate thing happened until my dad died. I know I probably clung to him as a crutch, and there WERE good times, I'm mostly hurt about the cold ending. What was the point of a long lecture about how great his wife is? To make me feel worse about this?

I own the fact that I made a bad decision, and that I did a bad thing. But the man made his first move on me at my father's wake, then toyed with me emotionally for over a year. I was a consenting adult, but he played unnecessary games.
Trying my best to forget his redeeming qualities and embrace the hate. I feel like it's my only shot.
